title: A member on a medical or travel freeze still shows up as 'stopped coming' and can get 'we miss you'
what: Freeze only moves the plan's last day later and writes a note. Nothing records that the member is away on purpose from today. So the Stopped coming list, the 'Stopped coming' message audience and the member's own 'we miss you' reminder all treat a frozen member like someone who quietly dropped out, and the owner is told to chase a person who is in hospital or travelling.
expected: While a freeze is running, the member is left off the stopped-coming list and its messages, and the phone does not send 'we miss you'.
who: owners, front desk and frozen members
how_often: every freeze for medical or travel reasons
fix_line: Store the freeze dates and skip the member in the away list, its messages and the phone's miss-you reminder until they end

title: The emergency number box refuses most landlines and two numbers, and saves a Bangalore landline as a wrong mobile
what: The emergency number box is built to keep a landline or two numbers as typed, but the save check then reads it as an Indian mobile. A Delhi or Mumbai landline (011 or 022 in front) or 'one number / another' is refused as 'looks wrong'. A Bangalore landline like 080 2345 6789 loses its 0 and is saved as the mobile +91 80234 56789, a number that does not exist, so a call in an emergency goes nowhere.
expected: The emergency number keeps a landline or two numbers as typed, or the box says plainly that only one mobile number is taken; it never turns a landline into a different number.
who: front desk adding members, and the member in an emergency
how_often: every member whose emergency contact is a landline or two numbers
fix_line: Check the emergency number with the same loose rule the box uses, and never strip the 0 from a landline

title: Money boxes refuse an amount typed in Hindi digits or pasted as 'Rs 1500'
what: The mobile boxes turn Hindi and other Indian keyboard digits into 0-9, but the price, joining fee and amount boxes on the sell and collect sheets do not. An amount typed on a Hindi keyboard, or pasted as 'Rs 1500' or '150,000', is refused with 'That amount looks wrong'. Nothing wrong is saved; the desk has to retype it.
expected: The money boxes take the same digits the mobile boxes take, and drop a leading 'Rs' or 'INR'.
who: front desk on a Hindi keyboard or pasting an amount
fix_line: Run the amount through the shared digit converter and drop a leading Rs before reading it
